source.title: A Stochastic Bundle Method for Interpolating Networks
source.authors: Alasdair Paren; Leonard Berrada; Rudra P. K. Poudel; M. P. Kumar

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out classification performance for adaptive optimizers and SGD on several benchmarks, using test or validation accuracy rather than the original studies’ measures.
record.gate_note: Optimizer comparisons bear on V4. The paper reports other optimization results, but does not test the other claim versions. It uses dropout at a fixed rate in one experiment; it does not compare dropout settings. Label-noise experiments do not test random-label memorization.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons using held-out classification accuracy, the same comparison and measure underlying V4. SNLI baseline results are explicitly reused from earlier work and are not independent tests by this study.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude that ALI-G provides competitive generalization with one learning-rate hyperparameter, while larger BORAT bundles improve robustness to learning rate and regularization, particularly with hinge losses or label noise. They describe BORAT as the most robust tested single-learning-rate-hyperparameter method, with generally similar generalization to ALI-G.
record.recipe_differences: Compares optimizer training recipes across standard benchmarks; adaptive methods are tuned and often compared with SGD using a hand-designed schedule, while some tables use constant-step-size SGD.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, architecture, loss, and whether the SGD comparison uses a manual schedule or constant step size change the optimizer ranking.
record.problems: Optimizer comparisons use different tuning procedures: SGD has a hand-designed schedule in some experiments, while constant-step-size SGD is used in the CIFAR comparison. Table 3 reports averages over three runs, but uncertainty is only available in the appendix for ALI-G and BORAT; several optimizer entries lack reported uncertainty. The study does not report training accuracy alongside these held-out results.
record.rows_left_out: Other optimizer and BORAT/ALI-G results in Tables 1–4 were not extracted when they were not needed to compare adaptive methods with SGD for V4. The CIFAR table’s Adam entries are absent; AMSGrad and AdamW are reported instead. The CIFAR-100 training-objective plots in Figure 4 do not report held-out performance.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under matched architectures and recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

Own language-benchmark Adam-versus-SGD results; word-level language modeling; worse held-out performance despite equal or better training performance; controlled effects of broader tuning, switching optimizers, or decoupling weight decay. Tuning also includes regularization and, on CIFAR, batch size.
Controlled batch-size comparisons at fixed epoch budgets and remedies for large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus equally sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. SNLI optimizer baselines are cited results, and its prose incorrectly suggests BORAT matches ALI-G on CE: Table 2 reports 84.4–84.5% versus 84.8%. CIFAR reversals against constant-step SGD do not challenge V4's full qualified claim. No matched training-performance comparison accompanies the extracted held-out results.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and generalization on natural labels.
Generalization as network width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Language benchmarks are included, but comparisons do not establish the effect of broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching from Adam to SGD as remedies; word-level language models are not tested.
No controlled comparison of batch sizes at fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout intervention or comparison of dropout settings.
No sharpness or other measure of the training–test gap.
No removal of memorized training examples.

relation.reason: The study reports adaptive-optimizer versus SGD held-out accuracy comparisons bearing directly on V4.

tranche.reason: The optimizer comparisons address V4 using held-out accuracy, but the method differs from its limited-tuning setup: regularization and sometimes batch size are tuned, and SGD uses either a manual schedule or a constant step size. The same outcome measure alone does not establish T1.

source_check.notes: The standard-deviation bound of 0.4 applies only to ALI-G/BORAT, not R9/R10. Tiny ImageNet uses WRN 16-4; its accuracy differences do not distinguish optimization failure from generalization differences at matched training performance.
